s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic inflammatory condition of the nails and mucous membranes with possible systemic involvement
salient_findings: Painful swelling of the proximal nail folds
Dripping of blood from fingernails and toenails
Occasional pus discharge
Lichenoid plaques and erosions on the oral mucosa
Violaceous discoloration and longitudinal ridging of the nails
key_facts: Male patient in his 60s
Symptoms present for the last year
No history of preceding trauma or drug intake
Raised liver enzyme levels
Positive anti–hepatitis C virus antibody status
Hyperkeratosis, hypergranulosis, acanthosis, and basal cell degeneration on histopathology
Dense bandlike lymphohistiocytic infiltrate in the papillary dermis
Numerous apoptotic keratinocytes in the epidermis
Nail changes include partial to complete loss of nail plate with oozing of blood and hemorrhagic crusting

shortlist.label: Lichen planus
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of painful swelling of the proximal nail folds, lichenoid plaques on the oral mucosa, and histopathological findings of hyperkeratosis, hypergranulosis, acanthosis, and basal cell degeneration

shortlist.label: Hepatitis C-associated lichen planus
shortlist.why_kept: Positive anti–hepatitis C virus antibody status and clinical presentation consistent with lichen planus

shortlist.label: Psoriatic nail disease
shortlist.why_kept: Nail changes include partial to complete loss of nail plate with oozing of blood and hemorrhagic crusting, which can be seen in psoriatic nail disease

shortlist.label: Dermatomyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Dense bandlike lymphohistiocytic infiltrate in the papillary dermis and presence of apoptotic keratinocytes, which can be seen in dermatomyositis

shortlist.label: Lupus erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic inflammatory condition of the nails and mucous membranes with possible systemic involvement, and raised liver enzyme levels

raw.rationale: The patient's positive anti-hepatitis C virus antibody status and raised liver enzyme levels, combined with the histopathological findings of hyperkeratosis, hypergranulosis, acanthosis, basal cell degeneration, and dense bandlike lymphohistiocytic infiltrate, are consistent with lichen planus. The association with hepatitis C virus infection further supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Lichen planus
rejected.why: While the histopathological findings are consistent with lichen planus, the presence of hepatitis C virus infection suggests a specific subtype.

rejected.label: Psoriatic nail disease
rejected.why: The nail changes and histopathological findings do not match the typical presentation of psoriatic nail disease.

rejected.label: Dermatomyositis
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and histopathological findings do not support a diagnosis of dermatomyositis.

rejected.label: Lupus erythematosus
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and histopathological findings do not support a diagnosis of lupus erythematosus.
